title: Kestrel and the Asset
premise: Ulyana Fairweather, a disgraced intelligence analyst haunted by a botched operation that killed his handler, receives calls on a burner phone from that same dead man's voice — a voiceprint of the training program's first successful 'asset,' kept alive as an experiment. Following the calls, he discovers the network that trained him never disbanded; it recycles broken analysts into deniable operators by rewriting their memories. To free himself and the asset — who is, in part, himself — Ulyana must burn the program's archive before a dawn extraction flight carries the last evidence out of the country. He succeeds at terrible cost: the archive burns, the voice goes silent forever, and Ulyana finally sleeps, carrying the memory he once tried to surrender.
about_author: N. M. Thackeray is the pen name of a former security consultant who spent a decade advising on data-retention policy for private intelligence firms before walking away. They write from a coastal town whose name they decline to publish.
